validity.researcher_notes: The line is real. A design institute table of Soviet trunk lines, a 2016 news story and the Ukrainian Wikipedia corridor article all name it. It is a trunk line (1000 mm, 5.4 MPa) from the Efremivka field area to Kyiv, built 1968 to 1970. It is a separate pipe from its two sister lines: Wikipedia and the design table give different diameters and years for each (700 mm 1961, 1000 mm 1970, 1220 mm 1973). It is not a duplicate. Length 477.8 km in the table against 477 on the sheet is within rounding. The Ukrainian Wikipedia article gives 1020 mm, the outer size of the same nominal pipe.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The newest evidence is a 2025 permit notice from Ukrgazvydobuvannya for the Efremivka field. It says field gas is sent into the Shebelinka-Dikanka-Kyiv or Efremivka-Dikanka-Kyiv line and on to the Khrestyshche compressor station. That describes current routing of gas, so the line is in use. The checker cannot read that file, so only the 2016 news story is staged as a ref, which is why the tier is low. Absence of other news is not evidence of closure. Status stays operating.
